title: serving-runtime-api-contracts-kv-scheduling-draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures an early API contract for the serving runtime surface that touches request semantics, error codes, and forward/backward compatibility rules. Focus areas: request schema, scheduling hints/priority, kernel capability negotiation, and KV cache semantics (lookup, writes, invalidation).

Goals:
- Provide a minimal, stable request/response shape for hosted + dedicated + private deployments.
- Make it possible for clients to opt-in to performance features (batching hints, cache keys) without breaking naive clients.
- Define clear error taxonomy so SDKs can map to retry/backoff and fallback policies.
- Define compatibility guarantees between control plane (API) and runtime kernel capabilities so rolling upgrades are safe.

High-level request shape (informal):
- request_id: string (opaque, provided by caller for tracing)
- model: string (model id, optional variant spec e.g., "llama-2-70b.quant-v2")
- model_version: string | null (if present, runtime must attempt that exact pinned version; else latest compatible)
- prompt: string | array of messages (supports both text and chat shapes; runtime accepts either)
- input_encoding: string (optional, e.g., "utf8", "llama-token"), if omitted runtime will autodetect
- max_tokens: integer
- temperature: float
- top_p: float
- streaming: boolean
- stream_format: string ("delta" | "chunked" | "json-lines") optional, only valid when streaming=true
- cache: object disguised via fields below (we only support flat top-level fields in this draft):
    - cache_key: string | null (client provided key to lookup KV cache)
    - cache_policy: string ("none" | "read-only" | "read-write" | "bypass-ttl")
    - cache_namespace: string optional (multi-tenant safety)
- scheduling_hints: (flat list in this doc)
    - priority: string ("low"|"normal"|"high")
    - latency_slo_ms: integer optional (best-effort hint to batcher)
- kernel_requirements: list-of-strings optional (e.g., ["fp16", "kv-compress", "fused-attn:v2"])
- trace_tags: list-of-strings optional
- client_metadata: string optional (opaque JSON in string form)

Notes on request shape:
- We intentionally keep a single-layer key space here so older SDKs can send unknown fields without breaking. The runtime must ignore unknown top-level fields.
- prompt can be either single text or chat structure; runtime must normalize and return canonicalized form in debug traces.

Response shape (summary):
- request_id: echoed
- status: string ("ok" | "error")
- model: resolved model id/version
- duration_ms: integer (server wall time)
- tokens_consumed: integer
- output: string or stream of chunks when streaming
- cache_hit: boolean optional
- cache_write_status: string optional ("written"|"skipped"|"error")
- error_code: integer optional
- error_message: string optional

Error taxonomy (early proposal):
Client errors (1000-1999):
- 1001: MALFORMED_REQUEST - missing required top-level field or invalid types- 1010: INVALID_MODEL - unknown model id or model not available to tenant- 1020: UNSUPPORTED_FIELD - client requested unsupported feature (SDKs should surface and fallback)

Transient/runtime errors (2000-2999):
- 2001: KERNEL_OOM - kernel ran out of memory, may be retriable with smaller batch/sequence- 2010: KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED - runtime cannot satisfy kernel_requirements; response will include supported capabilities list- 2020: INTERNAL_QUEUE_OVERFLOW - batcher/backpressure; clients should implement exponential backoff and optional fallback to lower-tier model

KV cache errors (3000-3099):
- 3001: KV_LOOKUP_FAILED - store read failed (transient)- 3002: KV_WRITE_FAILED - write failed (non-fatal, call may still succeed but cache_write_status set to "error")- 3003: KV_INCOMPATIBLE_SCHEMA - cached item incompatible with requested model version (cache must be invalidated)

Compatibility guarantees (draft):
- Backward compatibility: Runtime MUST accept request objects containing unknown top-level fields and ignore them. SDKs can add new optional fields without breaking older runtimes.
- Forward compatibility: Runtimes MAY return additional top-level response fields; older SDKs must ignore them.
- Model version pinning: If client supplies model_version, runtime MUST attempt to serve that exact model binary if available in that deployment. If unavailable, return error 1010.
- Kernel capability negotiation: Clients can declare kernel_requirements. Runtime will attempt to schedule on a node matching all requirements; if impossible, runtime returns 2010 with a list of supported capabilities in the debug trace. This is a soft-fail in the sense that runtimes MAY choose to ignore some optional capabilities (e.g., "kv-compress") and still serve, but MUST be explicit about which were honored.
- KV cache staleness: Cache entries are version-tagged with model_id+model_version+cache_schema_version. On lookup, if version mismatch -> return cache miss and set cache_write_status to "invalidated".

Scheduling semantics (how hints map to behavior):
- priority: high requests are favored for low-latency paths and smaller micro-batches. High priority may preempt queued normal jobs when necessary to meet SLO; excessive preemption will be rate limited.
- latency_slo_ms: hint to batching layer to form batch sizes that target that p99 latency. Batchers will use historical latency profiles to decide whether to send immediately or wait for more tokens/requests.
- best-effort batch hinting: clients can set "batching_hint":{"max_batch_tokens":int} in future; for now use latency_slo_ms and priority.

KV cache semantics (draft):
- Read path: if cache_policy in ("read-only","read-write") and cache_key present -> attempt lookup. If found and compatible -> return cached output with cache_hit=true and short-circuit kernel execution. If found but incompatible -> treat as miss and set cache_write_status="invalidated".
- Write path: if cache_policy is "read-write" and request completed successfully -> attempt write under cache_namespace and cache_key. Write failures are non-fatal (3002) and should not surface as overall call error unless explicit flag set in client_metadata.
- Eviction/TTL: cache entries must carry TTL and last-access. Default TTL is runtime-configured, typical value 24h for sequence-level caches. Clients can include a hint "bypass-ttl" to force revalidation (use sparingly).
- Atomicity: cache writes for the same cache_key are last-write-wins. No distributed transactions in this draft.

Kernel capability negotiation examples:
- Client requests ["fp16","kv-compress"] but runtime only has ["fp16"]. Response: 2010 with supported_capabilities:["fp16"], serve_can_fallback=true. SDK should decide whether to retry with modified kernel_requirements or accept fallback.

Error payload example (non-streaming):
{
  "request_id":"abc123",
  "status":"error",
  "error_code":2010,
  "error_message":"KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED: missing capability kv-compress",
  "supported_capabilities":"[\"fp16\",\"fused-attn:v2\"]"
}

Streaming error handling:
- If a streaming session encounters a kernel OOM after some chunks, the runtime will emit a final control chunk with status:error and code. Clients should gracefully close stream and optionally retry with smaller max_tokens.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should kernel_requirements be a bitmask (more compact) vs list-of-strings? (tradeoffs: readability vs wire-size).
- Do we expose cache diagnostics (hit reason, TTL remaining) in debug mode only? Concern: PII/leakage in multi-tenant.
- How to signal partial hardware degradation (GPU rack degraded) to clients as a soft signal for graceful fallback? Propose a capability "degraded:<level>".
- Define exact semantics for preemption fairness across tenants (rate-limited preemption tokens?).

Action items:
- Priya to prototype error->SDK mapping table (JIRA-RT-1020)
- Diego to add kernel capability discovery endpoint on control plane (GH: #430)
- Claire to align TTL defaults with Optimize team and surface config in console

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light on strict JSON schema to leave room for iterative rollout. Feedback requested on the error code ranges and whether KV errors should be fatal by default.

History / context:
- Pulls together previous notes from the kernels working group, the scheduling experiment we ran in Oct 2024, and KV cache RFC v0.3. See linked artifacts above for details.

Rough backwards-compatible sample request (non-streaming):
{ "request_id":"r-001", "model":"redwood:gptx-13b", "prompt":"Summarize: ...", "max_tokens":256, "streaming":false, "cache_key":"user-123:recent-convo-56", "cache_policy":"read-write", "scheduling_hints":"priority=high" }

End of draft.
